quest.title: A Librarian's Long and Carefree Vacation
quest.description: Effendi, the Akademiya's Liaison Officer, is looking for suitable volunteers for a long-term research project under the Spantamad Darshan...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Adventurer's Experience x2, Wanderer's Advice x4

dialogues.speaker: Effendi
dialogues.text: Greetings! Welcome to the Citadel of Regzar. Would you be interested in taking on some commissions?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are there any easy jobs where we can earn loads of Mora for just standing around? Oh, better yet, for sitting around! That's the kind of task we're interested in now.

dialogues.speaker: Effendi
dialogues.text: Uh, ahem... We don't currently have any commissions like that. However, I do have some relatively simple requests from residents that will pay several thousand Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really, that's all? That isn't nearly enough for Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Effendi, are there any high-paying commissions available?

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: Ah, I see. Let me think... Spantamad recently initiated a research project on the Ley Lines and is looking for paid volunteers.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: There are several researchers in Spantamad who specialize in studying Ley Lines, so there is a great demand for Ley Lines data. Researchers often need to enter Domains to investigate Ley Line Disorders.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: They have been understaffed for some time, even after recruiting a good number of their own students. So now they've turned to recruiting large numbers of volunteers.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: They offer substantial pay, but they also have strict requirements for the quality of the volunteers. Are you interested?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are the requirements?

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: Yes, let's walk through the recruitment process... First of all, "are you proficient with one or more types of weapon?"

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: Very good. "How's your understanding of elements? Are you capable of using elemental powers?"

choices.text: I know a lot about Elemental Reactions.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: Alright... I'll put you down as the Traveler, right? Okay, I've finished the registration. I'll be coordinating the necessary supplies and payments for volunteers later.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: You'll have to find Gafoor for more details about the job. However, he has an important visitor today, so I don't think he'll be in the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: According to the standard protocol for receiving visitors, he will most likely bring the visitor to the Puspa Café. You can go there and talk to him when his time with the visitor has finished.

response.speaker: Effendi
response.text: He sounded like he was in quite the rush to recruit volunteers when he contacted me, but now he's showing a visitor around. Seriously, who could be so important...?

choices.text: I am experienced at using elemental powers in battle.
Actually, I am proficient with all sorts of weapons.
We want something a little more lucrative.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: What a pity. It's very rare for us to meet like this.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Oh? Then would you like to spend some time with me, darling? That would be wonderful.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I plan to spend the next few days visiting around Sumeru City. At the end of my stay, I'll leave from Gandharva Ville and return to Mondstadt via Liyue.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Who knows, perhaps we'll bump into each other again in Sumeru City or Gandharva Ville.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hmm, come to think of it, there's something romantic about such a chance encounter like this. It's like icing on the cake for this little vacation of mine.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: If you see me around, be sure to come and say hello, otherwise I might start feeling lonely, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: There you are! Looks like you two are ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Very well. Let me inform you of some details.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Spantamad has been involved with the Ley Lines for a long time, and it's imperative that their current is constantly monitored. This research project was also organized to help meet this demand.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: However, because abnormal fluctuations often occur in Sumeru Domains, we must regularly send people deep into various Domains to record the situation with the Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Since it's often dangerous inside the Domains, we've established a rule of only dispatching personnel with combat capabilities.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: It'll be your task to go into the Domain and record any Ley Line anomalies. However, if you encounter any danger, please prioritize your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Well, those are all the necessary details. When you're ready, you may enter the Domain.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Do you still remember what the coffee's like here?
Of course, how could I forget? It used to be my go-to drink here.
Listen, Gafoor... Ahem, I suppose I should call you Professor Gafoor now... We're old acquaintances, so how about we stop beating around the bush, hmm?
First you wanted to catch up, and now the coffee... If you have something to say, just say it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's Gafoor. He's the one we're searching for, but he seems to be busy talking with someone else. Maybe we should wait for them to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Oh, well it's nothing, really. It's just that ever since you left the Akademiya, our original projects and plans have lost their backbone, so to speak.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: Cyrus is also disappointed. He's always valued you as a proud disciple.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: To be honest, it's a real shame that you left the Akademiya, Lisa.

dialogues.speaker: Gafoor
dialogues.text: With your wisdom and intellect, had you stayed in the Akademiya, you would have become a Herbad by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on... That's Lisa! The librarian Lisa! Our Lisa!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon heard that Lisa had studied at the Akademiya before, but that was a long time ago. What's Lisa doing here now?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: If I'm reading the situation right, you're reminiscing about the past to convince me to come back, aren't you?

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Well, I heard that you're currently the librarian for the Knights of Favonius in Mondstadt. If you ask me, that's a tragic waste of your talents.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Why waste your time and energy on something as trivial as taking care of a library? Your time is much more valuable than that.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: If you're willing to come back to the Akademiya, I have plenty of projects for you to preside over right away. The Akademiya needs people right now, and some of these projects are quite important...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Yawn... So all this talk IS to convince me to come back. I'm guessing Professor Cyrus doesn't know that you're talking to me about this.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: As a matter of fact, he has long wanted you to come back and work at the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: ...Is that so? You know, Professor Gafoor, it isn't a good idea to lie to people.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Our teacher knows exactly why I left the Akademiya after only two years. He would never ask me to come back.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Giving up my life in Mondstadt and returning to the Akademiya as a Spantamad researcher... The price of seeking wisdom is no longer something I'm willing to pay.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: So please, don't bother trying to get me to come back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so Lisa used to be a Spantamad researcher? Paimon's never heard her mention it before.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Besides, taking care of a library IS important work. I've never considered it a waste of my time.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: "Wisdom is hidden in every corner of the world. Never underestimate wisdom, no matter how small it may appear!" That's what our teacher always said.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: A good scholar wouldn't overlook the small details, Gafoor. *sigh* I'm sorry, I'm still not used to calling you "Professor." Nevertheless, the underlying meaning of what you just said is simply wrong.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: And there's one other detail you probably haven't noticed... Two people have been eavesdropping on us for quite a while now.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Is there anything we can help you two with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hello, Lisa!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Long time no see, Lisa.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Well, if it isn't you two.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Long time no see, cutie, Paimon.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Excuse me, but what business do you two have here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh well, actually, we're here to participate in a research project on Ley Lines for Spantamad! We just finished registering with Effendi.

choices.text: Which is when we happened to run into you, Lisa.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: A research project on Ley Lines? Oh darling, you haven't joined the Akademiya, have you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Only as project volunteers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, Effendi told us a research project is looking for paid volunteers. That's what we came to see Gafoor about.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Paid volunteers? Gafoor, is the Akademiya really that understaffed? Or are there projects that insist on the use of outsiders...?

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: No, no, the paid volunteers are for a conventional project to monitor the Ley Lines. All operations follow the prescribed safety protocols.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: We rely on a lot of manpower to collect the data; there's no way around it now. But if only you would agree to come back and preside over some matters, we wouldn't have to go through all this nonsense.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: If memory serves me right, collecting Ley Lines data requires investigators to go deep into Domains, which can be dangerous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've seen our fair share of combat since leaving Mondstadt! Exploring a Domain is like a walk in the park to us!

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: It's been so long now, I can only imagine what wonderful stories you have to share.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, so there's nothing to worry about.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Since you two are here to apply for the project, then please wait a moment while I talk to Lisa...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I'm sorry, Gafoor, my answer is still no.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Aren't you even a little bit interested?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I have never regretted my decision to leave the Akademiya... and I don't think that will change in the future.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: I thought after all this time, you would have a different answer. But you're still as obstinate as ever, Lisa.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: You've made yourself clear. I'll only make a fool of myself if I keep insisting.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: In that case, I still have unfinished business to take care of, so I'll take my leave. See you at the Darshan reunion in a few days.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Yes. Don't worry, I'll be there on time.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: As for you two, please come see me later in the Mawtiyima Forest when you're free. We'll need your help with the volunteer work.

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: Oh, and one last thing, Lisa...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Yes?

response.speaker: Gafoor
response.text: I wish you the best of luck in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: ...Thank you.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Well then, cuties, now that the recruiter is gone, we can sit down and have a good chat.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hehe, much has been happening within the Akademiya, and Gafoor is paving the way for his future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Lisa, what brought you to Sumeru? Are the Knights okay with you being gone?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Of course, Jean gave me an extended paid vacation. It's rare that I get any time off, so I thought to myself, "Why not go on a trip and relax a little?"

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I don't know how much of our conversation you heard, but I studied in the Spantamad Darshan at the Akademiya for two years.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: But instead of staying at the Akademiya after graduation, I went back to Mondstadt to become the librarian for the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why you came to Sumeru, right? To walk around and meet with your old friends and teachers.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why did you choose to leave the Akademiya?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: You'd like to know, wouldn't you? Well... I guess it wouldn't hurt if I told you. After all, it was ages ago.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: If anything, it all boils down to a difference in philosophy.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: When I first came to the Akademiya, Professor Cyrus really appreciated my work and invited me to participate in several major projects.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: But most of those projects ended in failure. To be honest, they went too far trying to achieve wisdom beyond mortal understanding, so failure was only to be expected.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I didn't want any part of that lunacy, so I left. Anyway, now that I told you, make sure you keep it between us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... sounds like you've experienced a lot.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I don't wish to return to the Akademiya, even if Professor Cyrus came to ask me personally.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Rather than conducting experiments day and night, I'm much more suited for working hours that start after 10:00 AM, with regular afternoon tea every day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhhh, Lisa chose to be a librarian because she doesn't want to deal with hassles all the time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That is Lisa's style.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I prefer to take things at my own pace when it comes to tiring tasks like a job. And besides, being able to take regular vacations is also really important.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: It's a pity I didn't even have time to visit that child in Gandharva Ville yet. Gafoor found me just after I arrived in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Speaking of which, what about you two? What brings my favorite cuties to Sumeru?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Lisa about all that's happened after coming to Sumeru.

choices.text: We didn't want to interrupt your conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I remember you two agreed to meet Gafoor in Mawtiyima Forest to talk about the Ley Lines research job.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Feel free to leave if you want to go look for him. As for me, I think I'll spend a little more time at Puspa Café.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I see... Even I didn't expect them to be so bent on their pursuit, wanting to even surpass the gods...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Sounds like you were involved in some remarkable events again, and I was completely unaware.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: And to think you were even able to handle a crisis of that magnitude... Cutie, your abilities are really beyond measure.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Having accomplished such a feat, I'm sure you must have a lot on your plate right now. I was actually thinking about inviting you two to walk around Sumeru with me...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I see... So you came to Sumeru in search of information on Lesser Lord Kusanali, the God of Wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: The two of you have more pressing issues than entertaining a tourist like me.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I wanted to walk around Sumeru with you, but now doesn't seem like the right time.
